raw_case_text:
An 18-year-old girl presented with a progressive bulging mass 2 x 3 cm2 in size, mildly tender, and soft without any fluctuation in 3 weeks located in her rib inter-space 1-2 near the left border of the sternum. She was living in the urban area and was healthy otherwise, except for a history of unpasteurized cheese usage. Intermittent low-grade fever (at night) and sweating were the only complaints. CXR was normal and ultrasonography reported the mass as a lymphadenopathy. Brucella seroagglutination tests, Wright, and 2ME were requested.
Laboratory data showed: WBC = 11,200: Neut = 78%, Lymph = 20%, Mono = 2%, Hb = 11.1, Wright = 1/640, 2ME = 1/80, ESR = 9. Other lab data were not remarkable.
Biopsy of the lesion showed nonspecific inflammation of the lymph node. She was treated with Cap. Doxycycline (100 mg/BID/Po) and Tab. Rifampin (600 mg/day/Po). After 2 months, lymphadenopathy disappeared and no relapse was reported after 1 year follow-up.
The third case was an 18-month-boy referred with a history of multiple, firm, and tender parasternal nodules (about 1.5 x 2 cm2 in size). He showed no constitutional symptoms.
There was no clear history of using unpasteurized dairy products. Wright and Coomb's Wright and all workups were negative. Routine laboratory exams revealed normal results. As a diagnostic approach, excisional biopsy was performed. Grossly, the lesion was cartilaginous with no evidence of necrosis or tumoral involvement. Microscopic examination revealed chronic nonspecific inflammatory process. The smear and culture of biopsied material were negative for tuberculosis or other bacteria. Due to persistent signs and symptoms, follow-up was done by repeated serologic tests which showed four-fold rising in brucella titer (8 weeks later). Treatment was started by Tab. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (trimethoprim, 8 mg/kg/Po) and Tab. Rifampin (10 mg/kg/Po) and continued for 8 weeks. Good response to therapy was achieved.

subjective.chief_complaint: Case 1: An 18-year-old female presented with a 3-week history of a progressive, mildly tender parasternal chest wall mass, nocturnal low-grade fever, and sweating. Case 2: An 18-month-old boy referred for multiple firm, tender parasternal nodules without constitutional symptoms.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Case 1: An 18-year-old female presented with a 3-week history of a progressive bulging mass near the left sternal border, accompanied by nocturnal low-grade fever and sweating. Case 2: An 18-month-old male presented with persistent multiple, firm, and tender parasternal nodules that failed to resolve, leading to excisional biopsy and subsequent serologic monitoring.
subjective.past_medical_history: Case 1: Urban resident, previously healthy; epidemiological history of unpasteurized cheese consumption. Case 2: No documented prior illnesses; no clear history of consuming unpasteurized dairy products.
subjective.review_of_systems: Case 1: Positive for nocturnal low-grade fever and night sweats. Case 2: Negative for constitutional symptoms. Home medications and allergies not documented for either patient.

objective.physical_examination: Case 1: Bulging mass measuring 2 x 3 cm^2 located in the left 1st-2nd intercostal space near the sternal border, mildly tender, soft, and non-fluctuant. Case 2: Multiple firm and tender parasternal nodules, approximately 1.5 x 2 cm^2 in size.
objective.routine_investigations: Case 1: WBC 11,200/mm^3 (neutrophils 78%, lymphocytes 20%, monocytes 2%), Hb 11.1 g/dL, ESR 9 mm/1st hour; CXR normal; ultrasonography reported the mass as lymphadenopathy. Case 2: Routine laboratory examinations revealed normal results.
objective.advanced_workup: Case 1: Biopsy of the lesion showed nonspecific lymph node inflammation. Case 2: Excisional biopsy revealed a cartilaginous lesion without evidence of necrosis or tumoral involvement, with histology demonstrating a chronic nonspecific inflammatory process; smear and culture were negative for tuberculosis or other bacteria.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Parasternal lymphadenopathy and chest wall granulomatous masses secondary to Brucellosis in both patients.
Confirmation:
Case 1: Wright agglutination titer of 1/640 and 2-mercaptoethanol (2ME) titer of 1/80.
Case 2: Initial Wright, Coombs-Wright, and routine workups were negative; repeat serologic testing at 8 weeks revealed a diagnostic four-fold rise in Brucella titer. Smears and cultures were negative for tuberculosis and other bacteria.
Treatment & Outcome:
Case 1: Treated with capsule doxycycline (100 mg BID orally) and tablet rifampin (600 mg/day orally) for 2 months; lymphadenopathy completely resolved with no relapse at 1-year follow-up.
Case 2: Treated with tablet trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (trimethoprim 8 mg/kg/day orally) and tablet rifampin (10 mg/kg/day orally) for 8 weeks, with good clinical response and complete resolution.
